text:
alice: FYI — spike time. Thinking about routing traces: we want Tempo as our long-term store (90d), Honeycomb for interactive high-cardinality debugging (30d hot window), and occasional Splunk/Datadog exports for enterprise customers. Need advice on OTEL collector setup, sampling, quotas, and how to avoid doubling ingestion costs when exporting to multiple backends.
ben: Yes you can configure multiple exporters in the collector, but naive fan-out will double/triple ingest. Two quick patterns: a) pre-sample + fan-out for important traces b) send a single copy to an internal proxy that fans out server-side (cheaper).
carol: +1 on proxy approach. Also consider tail-based sampling to keep high-quality traces in Honeycomb while storing everything in Tempo at lower fidelity. We use a tail_sampler + attribute enrichment (customer_id, route, model) so sampling decisions can use full span context.
dave: Security note — scrub PII before any downstream export. We should run the attribute processor to remove user_text and set masking rules. Also ensure exporters to third-party vendors use TLS and keys from KMS, not plain env vars.
ben: Example collector snippet (very rough):
```yaml
exporters:
  otlp/tempo:
    endpoint: tempo.internal.redwood:4317
  otlp/honeycomb:
    endpoint: https://api.honeycomb.io:443
  otlp/splunk:
    endpoint: https://http-inputs-prod.splunkcloud.com:443
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch, attributes, tail_sampler]
      exporters: [otlp/tempo]
# Note: honeycomb/splunk will be behind telemetry-proxy which applies sampling/rate-limits
```
carol: For routing, use the routingprocessor in the collector (or our proxy) to apply per-tenant rules. E.g. add attribute telemetry.route = "hot" for spans that should go to honeycomb/splunk. Then have routingprocessor/telemetry-proxy forward only those to additional exporters.
alice: How do we expose this per-tenant routing in the Console? We need a UX for "export destinations" per workspace + a way to toggle samplers/retention per workspace.
ben: Backend approach: store per-tenant telemetry policy in our config DB (telemetry_policies table). Have telemetry-proxy consult the service API (with caching) and apply sampling/routing. That keeps collector static and offloads dynamic decisions to a service we control.
dave: Also enforce quotas there — the proxy can throttle by tenant ID and emit quota-exceeded spans/events into internal monitoring. Audit log every time an exporter is enabled for a tenant.
carol: Operational gotcha: OTEL collector hot reload vs rolling deploys. Dynamic exporter changes via file-based configs + SIGHUP are fragile. Recommended: use a short-lived canary pool of collectors + telemetry-proxy to gate changes. Proxy lets us change routing without collector restarts.
ben: If we do want dual write sometimes (e.g., full stream to Tempo + selected to Honeycomb), implement dedupe keys in the backend or add an attribute like redwood.exported_by = "proxy-v2" so downstream can detect duplicates when necessary.
alice: What about cost/ingest visibility? Need token-level / tenant-level cost breakdowns in Console to show how much each exporter and retention window is spending.
carol: We can emit internal metrics from proxy/collector: spans_ingested{tenant,exporter}, spans_exported{tenant,exporter}, bytes_ingested. Wire those to our metrics pipeline and surface per-tenant dashboards. Also add alerts for sudden spike in spans_ingested.
ben: For testing, add a feature-flagged "telemetry_test" path that marks spans with test=true — allow us to route test traffic to a dev honeycomb dataset without touching prod.
dave: Compliance: ensure retention metadata is stored and enforced by proxy. If legal requests require deletion, proxy should be able to drop new writes and a background job prunes Tempo indexes (or calls vendor delete APIs where available).
carol: Mini-config for routingprocessor example:
```yaml
processors:
  routing:
    table:
      - from_attribute: "redwood.priority"
        to_exporters: [otlp/honeycomb]
      - from_attribute: "internal.tenancy" 
        match_type: "strict"
        to_exporters: [otlp/tempo]
```
ben: Ops suggestion — run a short canary: route 1% of traffic to honeycomb for a single tenant, validate dashboards and cost metrics, then increase. Have rollout steps in RFC.
deploy-bot: config-push: collector-config v2026-03-17a deployed to telemetry-canary group (ids: canary-3). Monitoring hooks enabled.
alice: Thanks — I'll draft an RFC with sections: objectives, per-tenant policy model, proxy design, collector config, sampling strategy, UX mockups for Console, and rollout plan. Will ping for reviewers. Next steps: ben to prototype telemetry-proxy fanout, carol to draft sampling + dashboard metrics, dave to write security + PII scrub checklist.
